subject.title: Model safety/alignment can block explicitly authorized operational tasks (e.g. SSH diagnostics)

question: Should OpenClaw add a narrow trusted-operator diagnostics contract for authorized read-only infrastructure work, or keep model/provider refusals terminal unless an explicit separate fallback policy is configured?
rationale: The remaining work changes how model safety decisions interact with operator authority and infrastructure tooling, so automation should not choose the policy boundary without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Define narrow trusted-operator diagnostics
options.body: Add an explicit security-reviewed contract and observability for read-only operational diagnostics without weakening destructive-command or hook-policy boundaries.

options.title: Diagnostics only, no execution bias
options.body: Improve refusal/tool/auth failure visibility while keeping model/provider refusals terminal and requiring manual operator retries or model changes.

options.title: Defer to provider-refusal fallback work
options.body: Let the narrower provider-refusal issue decide fallback behavior, leaving this broader SSH/operator-authorization contract unresolved.

recommendation.title: Define narrow trusted-operator diagnostics
recommendation.body: Add an explicit security-reviewed contract and observability for read-only operational diagnostics without weakening destructive-command or hook-policy boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest history-backed owner for the current refusal/failover surfaces and the policy boundary needs maintainer security/product judgment.
